title: How Long Does Dryer Vent Cleaning Take?
h1: How Long Does Dryer Vent Cleaning Take?
description: Most dryer vent cleanings take 30 minutes to an hour. Long runs, roof exits, bird nests or crushed ducts can add time. Here's what to expect on the visit.
quick_answer: A standard dryer vent cleaning usually takes about 30 minutes to an hour. Short, straight runs through an exterior wall are quickest. Vents that exit through the roof, long runs with several turns, heavy lint packs, bird nests, or ducts that need repair can push the visit to an hour and a half or more.
body:
What makes some dryer vents take longer?

The time depends mostly on how the vent is routed and what the technician finds inside it.

  • Length of the run: a dryer on an exterior wall with a short duct is fast. A laundry closet in the middle of the house with a long run through the attic takes longer.
  • Number of turns: each elbow is a spot where lint packs in and the brush has to work harder.
  • Where it exits: vents that end on the roof, common in two-story homes and many condos and townhomes, require roof access and careful work at the cap.
  • How clogged it is: a vent that hasn't been cleaned in years can be packed solid in spots.
  • Blockages: bird nests, rodent nests or a lost sock in the line add time.
  • Condition of the duct: crushed foil transition hoses or disconnected sections behind the dryer often need replacing.

What happens during a dryer vent cleaning?

  1. Pull out the dryer. The technician moves the dryer and disconnects the transition hose. Gas dryers need extra care around the gas connection.
  2. Inspect the run. They check the transition hose, the wall connection and the exterior or roof cap.
  3. Clean the duct. A rotary brush on flexible rods is run through the full length of the vent while a vacuum or air flow pushes lint out the far end.
  4. Clear the exterior cap. The damper flap or roof cap is cleaned so it opens freely, and any screen that traps lint is addressed.
  5. Clean behind and under the dryer. Lint collects in the dryer's lint trap housing and on the floor behind it.
  6. Reconnect and test. The dryer goes back, the connection is checked, and airflow is confirmed at the outside exit with the dryer running.

Signs your dryer vent needs cleaning

  • Clothes take more than one cycle to dry.
  • The dryer or the laundry room gets unusually hot.
  • You smell a burning or hot-lint odor during a load.
  • The exterior flap barely opens when the dryer is running.
  • Lint builds up around the outside vent or behind the dryer.
  • It's been more than a year since the last cleaning.

A clogged vent isn't just slow. Lint is very flammable, and a restricted vent makes the dryer run hotter and longer. If you smell burning, stop the dryer and don't use it until the vent has been checked.

Can I just clean it myself?

You can and should empty the lint screen every load, and you can vacuum behind the dryer. A store-bought brush kit can help on a short, straight run. Longer runs, roof exits and vents with several turns are where DIY brushes tend to get stuck or push lint further in. Roof work also comes with a fall risk.

If you have a gas dryer, don't disconnect or reconnect the gas line yourself. And if you ever smell gas, leave the house and call the gas utility from outside.

What should a good dryer vent setup look like?

While the technician is there, it's a good time to make sure the whole vent is set up right. A few things to look for:

  • A rigid or semi-rigid metal transition from the dryer to the wall, not white plastic or thin foil that crushes easily.
  • Enough space behind the dryer that the hose isn't kinked when the dryer is pushed back.
  • An exterior cap with a flap that opens fully and closes when the dryer is off, without a fine screen that catches lint.
  • A run that's as short and straight as the house allows.

If any of these are off, a repair or reroute during the same visit can make future cleanings quicker and the dryer more efficient.

How often should it be done?

Once a year is a good rule for most households. Larger families, homes with pets, and long or rooftop vent runs may need it more often. Our dryer vent cleaning team can clean, repair or reroute your vent and give you a time estimate when you book. Check current specials too.
faqs: Do I need to be home for dryer vent cleaning?
Usually, yes, since the technician needs access to the laundry area and the dryer. If the vent exits on the roof, they'll also need a safe way up.
Will the technician clean the inside of my dryer?
A vent cleaning focuses on the duct from the back of the dryer to the outside, plus the lint trap housing. Cleaning deeper inside the dryer cabinet is a separate appliance service.
Can a crushed dryer vent hose be fixed during the visit?
In most cases, yes. A crushed or plastic transition hose can be replaced with a proper metal one while the technician is there, which adds a little time.
Is a long dryer vent a problem?
Very long runs with several turns let lint build up faster and make the dryer work harder. Sometimes rerouting the vent to a shorter path is worth considering.
